sections.h2: Ways to sell a house in La Vergne
sections.html:
Selling in La Vergne means choosing among an agent, a sale you run yourself and a cash buyer who passes on the repair list. The house's condition and your deadline should steer that choice.

The city grew from 32,588 residents in 2010 to 42,146 by July 2025. Owners live in 74.0% of homes, those homes have a 2020-2024 median value of $309,900, and households average 3.03 people.

  • Agent listing: best for a house with few problems and an owner who can sit through showings and a buyer's loan approval.
  • Do-it-yourself sale: you keep the commission and also do the advertising and the contract work.
  • Cash buyer: works for houses with put-off repairs, a sitting tenant or an estate to close out.

The city lies in northern Rutherford County, southeast of Nashville, with Nashville's Antioch area to the northwest, Smyrna to the southeast and Percy Priest Lake to the northeast. Interstate 24 and U.S. routes 41 and 70S pass through. An average worker needs 31.6 minutes to reach a job.

Warehousing and distribution drive growth: an Amazon distribution center and the ICEE Corporation headquarters arrived in 2020, and a BJ's Wholesale Club in 2023. Lake Forest Estates, with more than 3,100 homes, is the largest single subdivision in Tennessee, so many sellers compete against similar houses on nearby streets.

Rutherford County Schools run the public schools inside the city, including LaVergne High School, LaVergne Middle School, LaVergne Lake Elementary, Rock Springs Elementary, Roy Waldron School and Simon Springs Community School. Zones can differ from street to street, so ask the district which school an address is zoned for before you tell a buyer.

Two separate tax bills apply here: the city's own and a county one from Rutherford County. Check that both are current. The Board of Mayor and Aldermen sets the city rate at $0.5363 on each $100 of assessed value.

County payments cannot be made at the city office. Send them to the Rutherford County Trustee, Judicial Building, Suite 302, Public Square North, Murfreesboro, 615-898-7705. Taxes more than two years overdue are handled by the Rutherford County Chancery Court at 615-898-7860. Clear any old balance before closing.

Code officers enforce upkeep rules from the city's Title 13 municipal code, and a buyer's inspector will spot violations. These come up often on resale houses.

  • Grass and weeds may not grow past one foot within 100 feet of a property line, residence or right-of-way.
  • A disabled or inoperable vehicle may not sit on the property for more than two weeks.
  • Swimming pools need a fence or barricade, and a pool permit costs $50 with a plot plan.
  • Unfit structures must be repaired or removed, or the city can step in.
  • Quiet hours run from 11:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.

Deck permits are $50 and shed permits depend on square footage. Electrical permits are state permits, and Rutherford County Building Codes at 615-898-7734 handles them. For anything else, the Codes Department number is 615-213-2624.

Buyers come for the water. Percy Priest Lake touches the northeast edge of the city, with boat launches at Hurricane Creek and camping at Poole Knobs Recreation Area. A 55-acre city park adds ball fields, tennis courts, a skate park, pavilions and trails, and it hosts the fall festival. A house within a short drive of either deserves a mention in listings and offer talks, because buyers can check those claims.

Selling is allowed, though the buyer should understand how the city treats the use. The zoning ordinance, updated July 7, 2026, defines a short-term vacation rental as a dwelling unit used entirely for transient occupancy, where the city has issued the owner a business license under the municipal code.

The use tables allow short-term vacation rentals in some districts outright and in others only with additional requirements, and the definition of residential use excludes rentals shorter than one month. Before you advertise a house as an income property, ask the La Vergne Tax Department at 615-793-3388 whether a business license is on file and what happens to it on a sale. The same office issues new business licenses.

The Rutherford County Register of Deeds files La Vergne deeds, not city hall. State deed transfer tax is 37 cents on every $100 of the price.

The Register's office does not run title searches and never guarantees that a deed is free and clear, so use a title company for that work. Its recording policy keeps overpayments of $10 or less per document, and a document with too little money attached is returned the same day. The office also hosts MyLandAlert, an alert service meant to flag land fraud early.

sections.h2: What to settle before a La Vergne closing
sections.html: Whichever buyer you choose, run through one short list. Ask the city tax office for a payoff figure, check the county bill with the Trustee in Murfreesboro and request a payoff letter from your lender. Then walk the property with the Title 13 rules in mind, because tall grass or an inoperable vehicle is an easy fix before an inspection. Cash needs no lender approval, so title work and your payoff set the date. Get it in writing.

sections.h2: A tidy sequence for the sale
sections.html: Start by deciding how much time you can spare. If you can wait, a listing in a city with this many similar houses needs good pricing and a presentable yard. If you cannot, a cash sale trades some price for a clear date. Next, collect paperwork: tax bills, a payoff letter, and permit papers for any pool, deck or shed. Last, hand all of it to the title company at the start, so the deed and recording at the Register go out without a second request.

faqs.q: Does a La Vergne seller owe the city tax at closing?
faqs.a: Yes, settle any unpaid city balance at or before closing, with proration worked out between buyer and seller. The La Vergne Tax Department can quote a payoff, and county taxes are a separate bill from the Rutherford County Trustee.

faqs.q: Where do I pay La Vergne property taxes?
faqs.a: City taxes go to the La Vergne Tax Department at 1500 E. Nir Shreibman Blvd., online through its tax search portal, or by phone at 877-580-5923. County taxes are paid to the Rutherford County Trustee in Murfreesboro.

faqs.q: Is there tax help for older La Vergne homeowners?
faqs.a: Yes. The city tax office has taken applications for the state's tax relief program for elderly or disabled owners and disabled veteran owners, and the tax freeze for seniors goes through the Rutherford County Trustee by appointment and must be renewed every year. Ask the Trustee for this year's income limit.

faqs.q: Who inspects electrical work in La Vergne?
faqs.a: State of Tennessee deputy inspectors do. La Vergne takes part in the state electrical program, so electrical permits are state permits, issued by Rutherford County Building Codes or through the state's online system.

faqs.q: What decides the closing date on a La Vergne sale?
faqs.a: Title work and your mortgage payoff set the pace, and a buyer paying cash does not wait on a lender. Get the closing date in writing and confirm with the title company that city and county taxes are paid.
